claims.statement: When a request-target is sent in absolute-form, an origin server MUST ignore any received Host header field and instead use the host information from the request-target.
claims.scope: HTTP/1.1 as specified by RFC 9112; applies to compliant origin servers and proxies processing absolute-form request-targets.

claims.statement: An attacker can cause a website to generate a password-reset link pointing to an attacker-controlled domain by manipulating the Host header used to construct that link, then capture the reset token when the victim (or an automated system) follows the link.
claims.scope: Applications that dynamically construct absolute URLs for password-reset or notification emails from the Host header (or a trusted forwarding header) without independent server-side validation.

claims.statement: An application may validate the literal 'Host' header against an allowlist while a separate code path reads a forwarding header (X-Forwarded-Host or X-Forwarded-Server) unvalidated, allowing the allowlist to be bypassed via the sibling header.
claims.scope: Deployments behind a reverse proxy where the proxy does not strip or overwrite client-supplied X-Forwarded-* headers before forwarding, and application code independently consults these headers.

claims.statement: Django's Host header parsing (django.http.HttpRequest.get_host()) in the affected versions incorrectly handled userinfo-style syntax in the Host header (e.g. 'validsite.com:random@evilsite.com'), allowing an attacker-controlled domain to be accepted and used to generate password-reset URLs.
claims.scope: Django versions affected by this historical parsing defect, prior to the corresponding framework-level fix; illustrative of a broader class of Host-parsing implementation bugs rather than a claim about current Django behavior.

claims.statement: If a caching layer's response content varies based on a Host-like header but the cache key does not include that header, a request bearing a manipulated header value can cause a poisoned response to be stored and later served to unrelated visitors requesting the same cached path.
claims.scope: Caching layers (CDN or reverse-proxy cache) placed in front of an origin whose response construction reads a Host-like header that is excluded from the configured cache key.

claims.statement: A client MUST send a Host header field in an HTTP/1.1 request even when the request-target is in absolute-form, to preserve compatibility with older HTTP/1.0 proxies that may not process absolute-form targets.
